claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Abstract: among TPMS topologies for cement, Lamella cuts mass 32% at 93% of solid compressive strength and 139.9% strength-to-weight; a generative ML model then synthesizes hybrid topologies reaching 104% of the best classical compressive performance.
claim.key_phrase: generative synthesis of hybrid topologies achieving 104% of the best classical compressive performance
claim.location: abstract (the only text accessible; full text could not be checked)
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Not applicable/not stated. The abstract reports only design-quality and structural-performance percentages (mass reduction, strength-to-weight, seismic response reduction); no computation time, iteration count, or cost figure of any kind appears in the abstract, and the full text could not be checked to look for one.
claim.alternatives: Abstract also reports 85-98% seismic response amplification reduction and 50-88% peak stress reduction across all seven topologies, and a predictive ML surrogate with R^2=0.987-0.999 (a fit-quality metric, not itself a classical comparison). Without full text it cannot be determined which single result the article itself treats as its headline comparison, or what its exact classical/control baseline is.

baseline.classical_method: not stated beyond an implied solid (non-porous) cement/concrete 'control' specimen and a 'classical' compressive-performance benchmark; no topology-optimization algorithm is named in the abstract (full text inaccessible)
baseline.solver: not stated; the abstract names 'Mazars continuum damage mechanics' for compressive/damage simulation and 'Newmark-beta' time integration for seismic simulation, but no software/solver package or classical TO algorithm
baseline.problem_size: not stated numerically as element/DOF counts; the abstract states 8,750 unique TPMS configurations were generated and evaluated across 7 topological families and porosity 0-70%, described as 'two orders of magnitude larger than prior studies'
baseline.data_generation_cost: not stated; the abstract states 8,750 configurations were simulated and top performers underwent seismic simulation plus a physical shaker-table validation, with no compute cost or time given
baseline.quality_metric: Compressive strength retention (% of solid), strength-to-weight ratio (% of control), tensile strength-to-weight ratio, seismic response amplification, and peak stress reduction, all named in the abstract; the verification method beyond 'Mazars continuum damage mechanics', 'Newmark-beta seismic simulation' and a 'calibrated shaker table' physical validation is not accessible
baseline.quality_gap: Abstract: Lamella (best single topology) retains 93% of solid compressive strength at 32% mass reduction, reaches 139.9% of the control's strength-to-weight ratio, and an '180x' improvement in tensile strength-to-weight ratio; all seven topologies show 85-98% seismic response amplification reduction and 50-88% peak stress reduction; a generative-ML hybrid topology reaches 104% of the best classical compressive performance

reporting.n_test_cases: not verifiable beyond the abstract's '8,750 unique TPMS configurations' and 'top performers' subset taken to seismic/physical testing; exact counts for later stages not stated
